title: Postern stream event payload
description: The JSON carried on a data: line of POST /postern/v0/stream. See SPEC.md section 4.3. Three of the five event types are defined here; done carries the run response (run-response.schema.json) and error carries the error envelope (error.schema.json), both already schema'd, so neither is repeated. The SSE framing itself — the event:/data: lines, start being first, exactly one done or error last — is not expressible in JSON Schema and stays in prose, with examples/stream.txt as the worked transcript. Every definition below is open: section 4.3's growth story depends on a client ignoring what it does not recognise, and this file constrains what a conforming runner emits rather than what a client must accept.

start.title: start event payload
start.description: MUST be first in a stream. Carries the run_id that the done payload repeats, which is how a client correlates a stream with its result and with the runner's logs.

run_id.description: Unique within the runner's lifetime (SPEC.md section 4.2).

step.title: step event payload
step.description: OPTIONAL, zero or more. name and status are what make a step event readable at all — one says which step, the other which edge of it — so both are required. model_id is absent for a step that calls no model.

latency_ms.description: The step's elapsed time, reported on finished. A runner MUST NOT emit it on a started step, where there is nothing yet to measure; a client that receives one anyway MUST ignore it rather than reject the event (SPEC.md section 4.3).

delta.title: delta event payload
delta.description: OPTIONAL, zero or more. Incremental output. If any delta is emitted, concatenating every delta.text in order MUST equal the final output.value — an invariant no schema can express, because it spans events rather than sitting inside one. scripts/validate.py asserts it against examples/stream.txt instead. A runner producing a bytes output emits no delta: the invariant is text-shaped, and base64 fragments would satisfy it while giving a client only the encoding to render (SPEC.md section 4.1.4).
